subject.title: feat: add lease-bound metadata to session spawns

question: Should OpenClaw expose this lease-bound external orchestrator session contract as a new core Gateway API, and if so what minimal stable API and storage ownership should it guarantee?
rationale: The PR adds a new privileged public control-plane contract, protocol discovery surface, and persisted state model; correctness fixes alone cannot decide whether that long-term core boundary is wanted.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core contract
options.body: Define the minimal supported Gateway methods, compatibility promise, persisted-state lifecycle, and upgrade proof, then request a narrowed implementation.

options.title: Provide a generic seam instead
options.body: Keep owner-specific orchestration policy outside core and add only the narrowly missing generic session or authorization extension point.

options.title: Decline this core direction
options.body: Keep the existing supported session tooling and route the external workflow through an integration-owned implementation.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Define the minimal supported Gateway methods, compatibility promise, persisted-state lifecycle, and upgrade proof, then request a narrowed implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: No current-main feature-history owner was available in the supplied read-only evidence; this reviewer has the strongest documented connection to the affected Gateway/session contract.
